rationale: Evidence: all 60 development trials across oval, s-bend and slalom ended off_track with zero completions. Max error sits at about 0.061 m, which is the off-track limit (max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4)). RMS error stayed near 0.027 to 0.030 on every track and in both iterations, and steering oscillation was low (0.06 to 0.20). The pattern is a persistent offset from the line, not jitter or instability. The most likely cause is the fixed left/right motor mismatch in the disturbance. With a proportional-only controller (ki = 0), that mismatch leaves a steady-state offset of roughly bias/kp, which pushes the robot toward the limit. Raising kp from 2.5 to 3.0 shrinks that offset. Adding a small integral term (ki = 0.4) removes it. The integral is clamped at +/-2, so windup on bends is bounded. Changes from iteration 1: kp 2.5 to 3.0, ki 0 to 0.4, kd 0.15 to 0.2 to damp the larger proportional and integral action, and base_speed kept at 1.2 so the change isolates the steering fix. Geometry and line_loss policy are unchanged so the race attributes the effect to the controller. Expected result: rms_error falls well below 0.027 and max_error drops below 0.06, so runs survive longer and progress rises above 0.3 on at least one track. Completion inside 3 s is still unlikely at this speed. Hypotheses to test: (H1) the failure is a steady drift from motor mismatch, so rms should drop with ki; (H2) if rms stays near 0.027 with ki, the cause is sensor geometry (outer sensors losing the 25 mm tape on bends), and I would widen the sensor spread or enlarge sensor_size next. Measurements wanted next: per-track progress, max_error location, line_loss_events, and whether oscillation rises with the higher kp.
